bullets.title: April PCE undershoots: core at 0.24% MoM, less hawkish signal amid war-driven dissaving
bullets.body: April core PCE came in ~4-5bps below consensus at 0.239% MoM, leaving the YoY rate at 3.3%; headline PCE 0.40% vs 0.5% expected. Personal income was flat (vs +0.4% consensus) and the savings rate dropped sharply from 3.2% to 2.6%, as consumers dissaved in response to oil price shock from the Iran conflict. Aggregate wage growth of only 3.5% YoY was flagged as the most dovish data point, with real PCE trending ~1.5% on a non-auto basis.

bullets.title: Fed expected on hold all year; 68% odds of zero 2026 cuts, 32% chance of a hike
bullets.body: Prediction markets put 98% odds on no change at the June FOMC and 93% for July; 68% probability of zero cuts in 2026 with 32% odds of at least one hike. Fed Vice Chair Jefferson expects inflation to decline as tariff effects and energy prices fade, while Governor Cook said she is prepared to support rate increases if higher inflation persists. Chicago Fed's Goolsbee warned AI productivity expectations could raise inflation and necessitate hikes.

bullets.title: ECB minutes hawkish: inflation risks up, growth down, rate hike on June 11 expected
bullets.body: ECB accounts show the vote on the last decision was close, with some members supporting higher rates; upside risks to inflation and downside risks to growth have both intensified. Energy price surge deemed significant and persistent, though second-round effects on consumers and wages remain limited so far. Eurozone headline CPI models point to 4.7% YoY by July vs the ECB's 2% target; first hike expected June 11. Eurozone ESI barely rose +0.3pts to 93.5, consistent with near-zero real GDP growth in Q2.

bullets.title: S&P 500 hits 20th all-time high of 2026; on track for 9th consecutive green week
bullets.body: The S&P 500 has recorded its 20th all-time high of 2026 and is on pace for its longest winning streak since 2023 at 9 consecutive green weeks. Fundstrat notes eight straight weekly gains have occurred alongside a new Fed chair and oil near multi-year highs, warning the six-month forward outlook may differ materially. JPM technicals flag the index as overbought but lacking evidence of imminent reversal; key support at 7,320-7,350 with 7,000-7,050 as a buy zone if a setback develops.

bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz escalation rattles crude and Middle East risk: vessels seized, missiles fired at Kuwait
bullets.body: Iran's IRGC seized two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, fired a missile toward Kuwait (intercepted), and US forces destroyed Iranian drones in the strait; CENTCOM called the ceasefire violation 'egregious.' IRGC declared it controls the strait and requires mandatory coordination for passage. The EU's Oil Coordination Group warned of a tighter jet fuel market within weeks if conditions don't improve, while JPM technical analysis notes crude threatening 82-84 support — a break would imply a reversion to 73.5-76.5 and act as a bullish catalyst for Treasuries and the S&P.

bullets.title: US macro data broadly net positive: strong capex, low claims, corporate profits +12% YoY
bullets.body: Q1 corporate profits rose 12% YoY with margins at 16.3%, up 2.8ppts from pre-COVID. Capex durable goods shipments were +0.4% MoM in April with tech capex up 2%+ MoM. Initial jobless claims remain historically low at ~210k trend; however, new home sales fell 6.2% MoM to 622k (near 2-year lows) with 9.4 months of supply, and Q2 residential investment was revised down to 0.6% SAAR. Morgan Stanley forecasts Q2 real spending growth at +2.2% QoQ.

bullets.title: US dollar forward rates shift meaningfully higher; wealthy families cutting USD exposure
bullets.body: USD 1-year forward rates have moved materially higher across the entire term structure vs. both one and three months ago. Separately, a UBS survey finds wealthy families are cutting USD exposure on US fiscal debt concerns, and JPMorgan's EMEA CEO stated the dollar will weaken structurally over the long term due to US fiscal dynamics.

bullets.title: Semiconductor rally may have overshot: sector trades at widest premium to 200-DMA since dot-com
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks are now trading above their 200-day moving average by the widest margin since the dot-com bust, and near-term EPS revisions have not kept pace with the rally. SOX is up ~75-82% YTD 2026, with chip stocks at ~26x forward vs ~90x at the dot-com peak. Key risk cited is a hyperscaler spending pullback or more efficient AI models.

bullets.title: AI token pricing war raises 'Groupon dynamics' concern; Goldman warns of race-to-the-bottom
bullets.body: Goldman's Delta One head compared the token economics of AI inference pricing to Groupon's subsidy wars: DeepSeek cut token pricing 75%, Xiaomi's MiMo cut pricing ~99%, raising concern about commoditization. Meanwhile, equity markets are pricing the strongest 5-year earnings growth in history, which macro strategists argue requires implausible nominal GDP growth (~10% per year, last seen in 1970s inflation).

bullets.title: Housing market deteriorating: home prices +0.7% YoY (slowest since June 2023), refi activity plunges
bullets.body: US home prices rose only 0.7% YoY, the slowest pace since June 2023; Hedgeye notes nominal prices +1.7% YoY (weakest since GFC) with real prices -1.6% heading toward -2.5-3.0%. MBA mortgage applications fell 8.5% WoW with refinancings down 18.1% as rates hit 9-month highs. April building permits were revised down to +4.4% MoM from +5.8%, annual rate falling to 1.423M units.

bullets.title: Consumer stress building: student loan delinquencies at 4-year high; CEO confidence retreats
bullets.body: 10.3% of student loan balances are 90+ days delinquent per NY Fed, the highest since 2020. Conference Board CEO confidence fell from 59 in Q1 to 47 in Q2, back into negative territory. Average new vehicle monthly payments hit $767 in Q4 2025; consumers with rolled-over underwater loans pay $916/month. ADP private payrolls slowed to 35,750 jobs/week from 40,750.

bullets.title: Energy Shock Monitor: US real gas consumption -13% YoY; global fuel prices +30% since conflict start
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Energy Shock Monitor shows US nominal gas station spending leveled off while real gas consumption is down 13% YoY. Global retail fuel prices are up 30% since the conflict began. Global flights underperform, particularly in Asia-Pacific and China, while global tanker imports are improving in Europe, LatAm, and Asia ex-China. Vehicle activity broadly holds but is weakening in Europe vs seasonal norms.

bullets.title: Mag 7 mostly lower in pre-market; MSFT outperforms on new AI coding model announcement at Build
bullets.body: Mag 7 opened the session mixed-to-lower: NVDA -1.1%, TSLA -1.3%, GOOGL -0.5%, AMZN -0.4%, AAPL -0.2%, META +0.2%, while MSFT outperformed at +3.0% on reports of new homegrown AI coding models to be unveiled at Build Conference, directly targeting Cursor and Claude Code competition. S&P futures were near flat with 10-year yields +1bp to 4.47% and WTI +2.1%.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley pivots risk-on: upgraded Small Caps, recommends barbell of Cyclicals + Hyperscalers
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Michael Wilson and Andrew Pauker called a durable market low in early April, subsequently recommending adding risk via a barbell of Cyclicals and Hyperscalers. They upgraded Small Caps to Overweight on November 17 when the cohort bottomed in relative performance. Russell 2000 is up 17.6% YTD, outperforming the S&P 500 by 7.8%.

bullets.title: JPM technicals: crude break below 82-84 would signal Treasuries rally and buy signal for Europe
bullets.body: JPMorgan's cross-asset chartbook notes December Brent has formed a bearish reversal below 93.00 resistance; a break below 82-84 would confirm a move toward 73.5-76.5 and allow Treasury front-end to complete a bullish reversal from the 4.09-4.11% zone. S&P Energy sector failed to make a new conflict-period high in May. EURO STOXX 50 held 5,745-5,750 support and could catch up to US if crude breaks. Gold expected to base at the 4,200-4,400 support zone.

bullets.title: Eurozone consumer confidence flat; services pick up but manufacturing, construction weaken
bullets.body: Eurozone consumer confidence was unchanged at -19.0 in May (final). Economic Sentiment rose +0.3pts to 93.5, slightly above consensus, driven by services (+0.8pts) and consumers (+1.6pts), while manufacturing (-0.3pts), construction (-0.8pts), and retail (-0.9pts) declined. Bund yields remain near 15-year highs and STOXX is at record highs but underperforming on a relative basis.

bullets.title: SpaceX files S-1 for SPCX Nasdaq IPO; $18.7B 2025 revenue but $4.9B net loss
bullets.body: SpaceX filed an S-1 for a Nasdaq IPO under ticker SPCX. 2025 revenue was $18.67B (+33% YoY) split across Space ($4.1B), Connectivity ($11.4B), and AI ($3.2B), but the company posted a $4.94B net loss as operating expenses surged to $21.3B from $13.6B. Q1 2026 revenue was $4.69B. Elon Musk holds 12.3% and joint executives/directors hold 20.2%; book runners include Goldman, Morgan Stanley, BofA, Citi, and JPMorgan.

bullets.title: AI concentration risk flagged: top 10 S&P names ~40% of index; investor positioning crowded in semis/hardware
bullets.body: 22V Research notes AI's biggest macro risk is rising market concentration and monopoly power rather than unemployment. Investor positioning is heavily concentrated in Commodities, Semis, Hardware, and AI infrastructure, with Software and Consumer Discretionary the least favored. The top 10 S&P 500 companies now represent nearly 40% of index weight.

bullets.title: NVIDIA's Jensen Huang teases undisclosed 'surprise product' at Computex; robotics and ARM PC chips in focus
bullets.body: Jensen Huang hinted at an unannounced Nvidia product at Computex; historically, every product he has teased has shipped and moved markets. Analysts point to ARM-based laptop chips (N1/N1X) competing with Intel and AMD, robotics/physical AI as trillion-dollar opportunities, and quantum-GPU integration as the most likely candidates. MS raises TSMC 2027 CoWoS capacity to 200kwpm from 160-170kwpm and frames Vera CPU as a $20B opportunity.

bullets.title: Caesars Entertainment (CZR) to be acquired by Fertitta Entertainment for $31/share, $17.6B total
bullets.body: CZR's board approved an all-cash acquisition by Fertitta Entertainment at $31.00/share — an 8% premium to last close and 49% premium to the Feb 25 baseline — valuing the company at ~$17.6B including $11.9B of assumed debt. The combined entity would include 60 casino resorts, William Hill sports betting at 200+ locations, and 600+ Fertitta outlets. A go-shop period runs through July 11; CEO Tom Reeg expected to remain.
